current.description: Cycle 15 makes the fleet aware of its OWN completion state and transition cleanly between WORK / MAINTENANCE / IDLE modes without wasting agent-passes. Cycles 10-14 closed the action loop (playbook runner, cockpit, model swap, re-routing, health scoring); cycle 15 adds mode-awareness: dispatch only sends open goals, idle seats get role-specific maintenance tasks instead of the generic menu, and the cockpit shows which mode the fleet is in. Three pillars: (1) Mode Controller - a single source of truth for fleet work-state (fleet-mode.json) read by dispatch + cockpit; (2) Dispatch Correctness - no agent is ever dispatched for a reached goal or handed a stale/generic task; (3) Idle Productivity - idle passes must still produce a file/measurement/evidence, and the fleet measures its own productive-pass rate. Every seat's goals advance at least one pillar.

past.description: Cycle 10 closes the loop between intelligence and action. Cycle 9 built the sensing layer (forecasts, health scores, collaboration graphs); cycle 10 makes the fleet act on its own observations without waiting for a human pass. Three pillars: (1) Auto-Remediation - when a degradation is detected, the fleet executes the fix (model swap, host failover, task re-route) and logs the decision; (2) Self-Balancing - workload distribution, model routing, and context management optimize themselves based on live throughput data; (3) Fleet Cockpit - a single unified view (portal + API) that shows all fleet state in real time: agent status, goal progress, resource usage, recent decisions, and predicted risks. Every agent's goals should advance at least one pillar.

Cycle 9 shifts the fleet from reactive productionization to proactive, self-optimizing behavior. Goals focus on: (1) predictive operations - anticipating failures and resource needs before they occur, (2) knowledge synthesis - building a shared semantic layer so agents can reason over fleet state without re-deriving context each pass, (3) delivery value - making the portal and fleet produce outputs a human would find useful (reports, insights, automated decisions). Each agent's 10 goals should advance at least one of these three pillars.
